summary:
Turn 20 resumed the paused accept-status Candidate (distinct responsibility, A2) after the map handoff was accepted as version 5.

Why this question now. The surrounding reachability questions are decided: the TryPreAccept path and findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut are unreachable dead code, and recovery sub-case 2 can be reached only through the record of a replica that led the instance, because the leader-side accept branch is the one place that stores ACCEPTED together with the merged attributes. An accept-only acceptor therefore never reports an accepted status, and the newly confirmed recovery checks give the outcome shape that this question would predict: a NOOP vector committed for an instance another replica holds as COMMITTED. That makes the accept-only acceptor's command-less reply at the accepted vbal the natural next discriminator rather than another variant of the closed recovery-vbal finding.

Product. The Candidate is resumed on its stored proposition verbatim (its basis is not reinterpreted), with refined unknowns: whether the recovery value selection can prefer an accept-only acceptor's command-less reply at the accepted vbal over an equal-vbal reply that carries the value, given the last-element-at-or-above-the-running-maximum rule; whether the missing ACCEPTED transition changes any decision now that the only other status shortcut is dead; and whether the intended acceptor discipline is fixed by a source outside this snapshot. The work that would justify pausing it again is recorded in the remaining list rather than as resume conditions, since the action resumes the candidate (the validator rejects resume conditions for a non-paused candidate). The confirmed recovery finding is cited as an analogue, not folded in, so the distinction between a leader that ignores a reported commit and an acceptor that never records that it accepted stays intact.
